main_point: It's about whether the discovery rule works for software; I couldn't tell what the author wanted courts to do until Part III.

look_for.item: The claim and the contribution, stated in the introduction's first few pages
look_for.quote: This Article explores how the discovery rule applies to software defects

look_for.item: A roadmap that matches the Parts that follow
look_for.quote: Part III develops a framework for software accrual. Part IV responds to objections.
look_for.note: Part III proposes a rule, not a framework, and there's no Part IV.

look_for.item: Background sized to what the argument needs, not a survey of the whole area
look_for.quote: Part I traces the history of the discovery rule.
look_for.note: Part I is the longest Part; I needed two paragraphs of it.

look_for.item: Stakes that reach beyond specialists in the subfield
look_for.quote: Software now runs the locks on our doors, the brakes in our cars, and the pumps that deliver insulin.
look_for.note: The stakes land for any reader.

look_for.item: Subfield terms and acronyms explained at first use
look_for.quote: Under the discovery rule, a claim does not accrue until the plaintiff knew or reasonably should have known of the injury and its cause.
look_for.note: The key doctrine is explained in one sentence.

look_for.item: Each Part's opening saying what that Part does for the argument
look_for.quote: The discovery rule has a long pedigree.
look_for.note: Part I opens with history, not with why the history matters here.

findings.quote: This Article explores how the discovery rule applies to software defects and what courts should make of the manufacturer's power to change the product after the sale.
findings.why_it_matters: I decide whether to keep reading at the end of the introduction, and 'explores' tells me there's no position yet.

findings.quote: Part III develops a framework for software accrual. Part IV responds to objections.
findings.issue: The roadmap promises a framework and a Part IV the draft doesn't have
findings.why_it_matters: I trusted the roadmap and went looking for objections that aren't there.

findings.quote: The discovery rule has a long pedigree.
findings.issue: The history Part is longer than the argument
findings.why_it_matters: I skimmed most of Part I; the one point I needed, that the rule assumes a fixed product, is in its last paragraph.

findings.quote: Second, the rule is administrable. Patch notes are dated and public.
findings.issue: The opening story never comes back to test the rule
findings.why_it_matters: I'd find the proposal more convincing if I saw it decide the Keystead case. When would the first family's clock have started?

findings.quote: [Part II.C to come: survey of state statutes of repose and how they treat updates]
findings.why_it_matters: A reader at the workshop will see an unfinished section.

what_works.note: The best sentence in the draft. I'd want it right after the opening story.

what_works.quote: On a cold night in January, a family in Rivermont woke to find their front door standing open.
what_works.note: An opening that makes me keep reading.
